subject: Renewal proposal: transition to 16 GPUs and updated monthly commit
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna@neuroscale.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: transition to 16 GPUs and updated monthly commit

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our roadmap review, it sounds like NeuroScale will need a predictable uplift in inference throughput over the next 12 months. To make sure we’re aligned ahead of your renewal, I put together a concise proposal to update your Dedicated pool from 8 → 16 GPUs and adjust the monthly commit accordingly. Attached is a pricing schedule and a draft amendment for procurement to review.

Key highlights: 
- Capacity change: reserved pool increased to 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs.
- Monthly commit: new baseline to be 2.2M token units/month (phased billing option available).
- Throughput SLOs: 95th percentile tail latencies preserved for existing instance classes; we’ll include throughput guardrails in the amendment.
- Activation: phased activation over two weeks to minimize cold-start risk; ops playbook included.

Would love to lock a short call this week to walk procurement/ops through the amendment and timing. Proposed times: Tue 10:00–11:00PT or Wed 14:00–15:00PT.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly invoicing).
2) Procurement reviews draft amendment and highlights any redlines.
3) Ops sync to validate activation runbook and network/VPC setup.

I’ve CC’d David (solutions) and Marissa (customer success) to coordinate the technical activation and onboarding checklist.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

Attachments: Redwood_NeuroScale_16GPU_pricing_schedule_v3.pdf (price table), Draft_Amendment_8to16.docx (redline-ready)
From: Anna Li <anna@neuroscale.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@neuroscale.ai, ops@neuroscale.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: transition to 16 GPUs and updated monthly commit

Jordan —

Thanks for the thorough proposal and the attachments. A few quick items from our side before we schedule a call: 

1) Procurement asks whether the monthly commit increase to 2.2M token units includes any burst capacity or if burst is billed separately. They prefer a single committed amount if possible.
2) Ops wants a concrete throughput guarantee for our inference peak window (US morning hours). Can you confirm sustained QPS per model shard for the 16-GPU pool?
3) We’ll likely need a 30-day SOC2 evidence package and a short runbook for the phased activation — ops copied here.

We’re generally aligned on the capacity uplift, but procurement would also like a cost/benefit snapshot vs keeping 8 GPUs + on-demand bursts for peak times.

If you can address the three bullets above, I’ll get procurement to review the draft amendment and propose a preferred signing timeline.

Cheers,
Anna Li
Head of Platform, NeuroScale
anna@neuroscale.ai

Folks —

Looping in some of the operational detail Anna requested so Jordan can forward to NeuroScale. Notes below are concise so we can put them into the runbook and amendment: 

- Burst vs committed: The 2.2M token/month commit is the guaranteed baseline. We can bundle a small burst buffer (equivalent to ~15% extra capacity) into the plan at a fixed uplift; otherwise bursts are billed at overage rates. Recommend we offer a 15% burst buffer for the first 3 months to smooth the cutover.

- Sustained throughput: With 16 GPUs and the model mix you described (2 primary model shards, average seq len 128), we can target sustained 1.8–2.2k QPS aggregate depending on batching. We’ll include a per-shard target in the SLO table; exact numbers will need a quick smoke run during the activation window.

- SOC2 evidence: Marissa — can you prepare the 30-day package (SOC2 cert summary, recent penetration test, retention policy excerpt)? We’ll attach that link to the amendment.

- Activation playbook: Proposed two-week phased activation: week 1 — warm-up + prefix caching; week 2 — full traffic migration with canary routing (10% → 50% → 100%). Ops checks: VPC peering, KMS key access, network egress rules, and monitoring alerts.

I’ll draft the SLO bullets for Jordan to send.

-David
David Kim
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Anna / team —

Thanks — appreciate the quick feedback. Below is a short mutual action plan (MAP) we can all use to keep momentum: 

1) Commercial: I’ll update the draft amendment to include an explicit 15% burst buffer for the first 90 days at a fixed uplift. Procurement to confirm whether they still prefer a single committed SKU or will accept the uplift line item. Target: Procurement sign-off by 2026-03-24.

2) Ops: David and I will run a 2-hour smoke test during the activation week to validate the 1.8–2.2k QPS band. Ops to confirm dates (suggest 2026-04-05 or 2026-04-07). Marissa will assemble the SOC2 evidence bundle and the activation checklist.

3) Billing/Legal: I’ve attached the updated pricing schedule and a draft amendment (v3). If procurement confirms the single-SKU preference, we’ll roll that into v4 for signature. I’ll also open a HubSpot task and a DocuSign envelope; links below.

Action items: 
- Jordan: send updated amendment (v4) with procurement preference applied — by 2026-03-18.
- Procurement (NeuroScale): review amendment and indicate billing cadence preference — by 2026-03-22.
- David/Ops: confirm smoke test date and provide runbook — by 2026-03-25.
- Marissa: upload SOC2 evidence and activation checklist to shared Drive — by 2026-03-19.

If that timeline looks good, I’ll book a 30-minute alignment call for Thu 2026-03-18 10:00 PT and send calendar invites.

Best,
Jordan
